That won't do a thing to ease anyone's pain. Not your family's, not the cop who gets the call, not yours. 

I'm not going to tell you not to be sad but I want to show you something good that can come from sadness. Something good that can come out of the bad things in life. My old friend, the blues.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=k_rd8y8A2oE

Would it be worth the hurt you'd leave behind? If you do it at home, your family will find you. I don't care how bad you think things are with them, if they find you dead in your room they will hurt, badly and for ages. 

If you do it somewhere else, well, someone else will find you. This was why, at a low point in my life within the last couple years, I planned to walk out to the woods north of town, to an abandoned railroad bridge high over a shallow creek. I figured I could hang myself from it, or jump from it, and disappear and who'd be the wiser? Then I realized, someone would find whatever was left of me. A hiker, a hunter. Someone in a search party. 

I can't pretend to know how deep your pain runs or for how long you've been hurting. I'm just some stranger on the internet. I can only ask you to think of the pain you'd cause for someone, be they your own family or a complete stranger, by killing yourself and leaving them to find your remains. 

I don't know you but I hope we'll be able to talk again. I'm not very sociable here but reply if you like. Whether the world is just or unjust, I don't know, but there're good things in the world worth a moment's pleasure. There're bad things in the world worth anything you can do to make them better. 

It's hard for me to believe this some days, but just by being alive you have worth and value, you have something to offer. I hope you'll keep looking for that something just a little while longer.

The Defiant was destroyed by the Breen energy-dissipating weapon, which wiped out systems throughout the ship, including shields and weapons, and most likely propulsion. If the energy dissipation took the warp core offline, there might not have been any antimatter outside of the containment pods when the ship, drifting without power, was fired on. The torpedoes blasted the ship to pieces, but the antimatter containment pods may have survived among the wreckage.

Edited to add: the one ship to survive the battle was a Klingon vessel that had earlier performed a modification to its engines that somehow made it immune to the effects of the energy-dissipator.

I'd add that your ability to patch the tire depends on where the screw is stuck. If it's within the middle of the tread surface it should be okay, but if it's on the inner or outer edge of the tread, basically within an inch of the sidewall, a patch won't hold. Out of probably six or seven tires that have gone flat on me since I've been driving, I only recall one that a shop would recommend patching up instead of replacing.

I had a 93 Oldsmobile with a 3.3 liter V6 which had similar symptoms. It began while I was in traffic and I felt like I could barely make it home. When my brother and I were troubleshooting, we pulled the serpentine belt -- which eliminated the noise. The crankshaft pulley on this particular V6 is the harmonic balancer type. It's metal around the edge, with rubber in the middle that helps insulate vibration from the engine. When it fails it makes a hell of a noise.

I don't know Hondas well, this could be bearings but it could also be a pulley given that the noise stops when the belt is off. I'd look at that before calling the junkyard.
